 BMKG Head Teuku Faisal Fathani at the Presidential Palace in Jakarta on Wednesday (21/10/2026). (Adhyasta Dirgantara) 
 JAKARTA, KOMPAS.com -  The Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) predicts that Indonesia will enter the rainy season in November to December 2026, later than the usual cycle.
 BMKG Head Teuku Faisal Fathani noted that with the delayed prediction for the start of the rainy season, the peak is expected to occur from December 2026 to February 2027.
 "If it starts in November to December, the peak will occur in December, January, and February," said Teuku at the Presidential Palace Complex in Jakarta on Monday (26/10/2026).
 He also mentioned that this year's rainfall duration will be shorter than in previous years.
 Moreover, he explained that the delay in the rainy season is due to the El Niño phenomenon.
 "The average entry of the rainy season across Indonesia is expected to be delayed by about two to three decades, or 20–30 days, due to the influence of El Niño," Teuku stated.
 Nevertheless, Teuku cautioned about the potential for hydrometeorological disasters such as floods and landslides during the upcoming rainy season peak.
 "From the end of this year to the beginning of next year, we need to be vigilant about wet hydrometeorological disasters," he said.
 Teuku visited the Palace to attend a limited meeting with President Prabowo Subianto regarding handling forest and land fires and the potential for hydrometeorological disasters.
 "We have also prepared a lot of materials, from updates on forest fires and how El Niño will develop in the future, to preparations for facing hydrometeorological disasters," he added.
